\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ارث} \fa{بردن} (ers bordan)}{ارث بردن (ers bordan)}]{\fa{ارث} \fa{بردن} (ers bordan) — to inherit}

\label{lesson:FA-C506-ers-bordan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to hug, then the Persian for to caress.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ارث} \fa{بردن}}
\textbf{\fa{ارث} \fa{بردن}} (\emph{ers bordan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{این} \fa{خانه} \fa{را} \fa{از} \fa{پدربزرگش} \fa{ارث} \fa{برد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u in khâne râ az pedarbozorgash ers bord.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He inherited this house from his grandfather.
\end{quote}

\emph{ers} 'inheritance' + \emph{bordan} 'to carry off'; present stem \emph{bar-}. The giver takes \emph{az}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ers} is a loan, usually traced to the Arabic word for 'inheritance'; EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{bordan}, 'to carry', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ers bordan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ers bordan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ers bordan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to hug, then the Persian for to caress, then say \emph{ers bordan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شباهت} \fa{داشتن} (shebâhat dâshtan)}{شباهت داشتن (shebâhat dâshtan)}]{\fa{شباهت} \fa{داشتن} (shebâhat dâshtan) — to resemble, to look like}

\label{lesson:FA-C506-shebahat-dashtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to caress, then the Persian for to inherit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شباهت} \fa{داشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{شباهت} \fa{داشتن}} (\emph{shebâhat dâshtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to resemble, to look like\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{خیلی} \fa{به} \fa{مادرش} \fa{شباهت} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u kheyli be mâdarash shebâhat dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She looks a lot like her mother.
\end{quote}

\emph{be kasi shebâhat dâshtan}; \emph{shebâhat} 'likeness' + \emph{dâshtan} 'to have'. It shares a root with \emph{shabih} 'similar'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shebâhat} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{šabāha}, 'likeness', from the same root as \emph{shabih}, 'similar'. EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{dâshtan} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shebâhat dâshtan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{shebâhat dâshtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to caress, then the Persian for to inherit, then say \emph{shebâhat dâshtan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سر} \fa{زدن} (sar zadan)}{سر زدن (sar zadan)}]{\fa{سر} \fa{زدن} (sar zadan) — to drop in (on someone)}

\label{lesson:FA-C506-sar-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to inherit, then the Persian for to resemble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سر} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{سر} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{sar zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to drop in (on someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{کار} \fa{به} \fa{مادرم} \fa{سر} \fa{میزنم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ba'd az kâr be mâdaram sar mizanam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After work I drop in on my mother.
\end{quote}

\emph{be kasi sar zadan}; literally 'to strike a head'. Present stem \emph{zan-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sar zadan} is built on two inherited words: \emph{sar}, 'head', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{zadan}, 'to strike'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to inherit, then the Persian for to resemble, then say \emph{sar zadan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رفت} \fa{و} \fa{آمد} \fa{کردن} (raft-o âmad kardan)}{رفت و آمد کردن (raft-o âmad kardan)}]{\fa{رفت} \fa{و} \fa{آمد} \fa{کردن} (raft-o âmad kardan) — to visit each other, to keep in touch}

\label{lesson:FA-C506-raft-o-amad-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to resemble, then the Persian for to drop in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رفت} \fa{و} \fa{آمد} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{رفت} \fa{و} \fa{آمد} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{raft-o âmad kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to visit each other, to keep in touch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ما} \fa{با} \fa{همسایه} \fa{ها} \fa{زیاد} \fa{رفت} \fa{و} \fa{آمد} \fa{میکنیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâ bâ hamsâyehâ ziyâd raft-o âmad mikonim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We see a lot of our neighbours.
\end{quote}

\emph{raft} 'going' + \emph{o} 'and' + \emph{âmad} 'coming' (the past stems of \emph{raftan} and \emph{âmadan}) + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{raft-o âmad} is built on two inherited past stems, \emph{raft} from \emph{raftan}, 'to go', and \emph{âmad} from \emph{âmadan}, 'to come': coming and going. \emph{kardan} is inherited too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{raft-o âmad kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to resemble, then the Persian for to drop in, then say \emph{raft-o âmad kardan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آبرو} (âberu)}{آبرو (âberu)}]{\fa{آبرو} (âberu) — reputation, good name}

\label{lesson:FA-C506-aberu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to drop in, then the Persian for to visit each other.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آبرو}}
\textbf{\fa{آبرو}} (\emph{âberu}) — \textquotedblleft{}reputation, good name\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{کار} \fa{آبروی} \fa{خانواده} \fa{را} \fa{برد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in kâr âberu-ye khânevâde râ bord.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This act disgraced the family.
\end{quote}

\emph{âberu bordan} — to disgrace; \emph{âberu dâshtan} — to be respected.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âberu} is built on two native Persian words: \emph{âb}, 'water, lustre', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{ru}, 'face': the shine on a face.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
